feedback.answered: The in-repository InteractionEnv is now inspected rather than assumed external: synchronous ProcessReady calls processAppend and processApply before publishing messages and Advance. Async ProcessAppendThread dequeues append work FIFO, writes it, then exposes attached responses; ProcessApplyThread applies each configuration through RawNode.ApplyConfChange, updates appender-state history and only then exposes responses. Thus these adapters implement a stricter completion schedule than Node early Advance and do not exercise the admitted overlap. Their processAppend also notes its HardState-before-entries order is not necessarily crash-safe, and ProcessReady explicitly does not simulate crashes, so successful adapter tests cannot establish crash durability ordering. The Message interface defines append-response index/term as stability by completion of the associated append work, potentially referring to entries from earlier work; it does not authorize premature network publication. README and package prose still permit sending same-batch messages during entry persistence while Ready requires entries first, so the contract conflict remains. For the separate postponed-read surface: with actual ApplyConfChange completed before Advance, hup refuses campaigns with unapplied committed configuration; if a prior-term configuration is initially uncommitted, current-term commitment through append acknowledgment releases pending reads before its application. These protections explain why an arbitrary switchToConfig state injection is not a legal witness. This is a conditional source explanation only: the demonstrated Node early-Advance bookkeeping gap leaves broader legal application/election histories unresolved.
